items.excerpt: CDM spots an emerging scene of producers deliberately recording strange or 'bad' music in the hope AI scrapers will train on it — data poisoning as a creative genre. A craft-level response to generative models that turns the training pipeline itself into material.

India's oldest label Saregama is using generative video to build music videos for catalog songs whose original visuals it never owned, repackaging the archive for Gen Z. A concrete case of AI video production replacing an asset the rights holder simply never had.

KOMCA's amended rules took effect August 3, ending South Korea's blanket ban on registering AI-assisted songs — but writers must now declare AI use, with false filings risking royalty holds and contract termination. Changes how Korean songwriters document an AI-touched session.

MBW columnist Sammy Andrews argues the unspoken AI fight in music isn't over who owns the output but over who shapes demand — distribution versus desire. Frames what creative teams should actually be designing for as generative supply becomes infinite.

Music Ally revisits Fenix Flexin's viral 'Rubberz' and the accusations that it is AI-generated, pulling apart why the question is now almost unanswerable when most DAW tools already embed AI. A useful test case for where 'AI-assisted' ends and 'AI-generated' begins.

A Billboard-charting single is widely suspected of being AI-generated while the credited rapper denies it, with critics pointing to 'telltale' artifacts in the production. Detection-by-ear is becoming a working skill for listeners and A&R alike.

Daft Punk's Thomas Bangalter says he's 'not really interested in the creative usage of AI', in a rare sit-down interview. A pointed counterweight from one of electronic music's most machine-obsessed producers about where the tool stops being interesting.
Empire Of The Sun's Luke Steele says 'of course' he uses AI and warns artists who refuse it risk being swallowed by it. A working songwriter putting the adopt-or-resist question on the record.

DMN assesses Google's Flow Music Spaces update — song generation and editing, stem splitting, lyrics, artwork and video in one workspace — and asks whether Google is assembling the first genuinely all-in-one AI music studio. The consolidation story matters more than any single feature.

A London 'sound-free concert' used generative AI music platforms plus Bluetooth-connected cochlear implants to stream audio directly to d/Deaf attendees. Generative music as an accessibility design surface rather than a content firehose.
A Kapwing study finds the top 10 AI music acts have pulled roughly $6.1m from over 2.3 billion streams and views. AI 'artists' have moved past novelty into a working release-and-audience playbook.

Majors and indies jointly proposed chart-eligibility rules for AI: only AI-assisted tracks may chart, only legitimate AI tools may be used, and AI use must be labelled. A labelling standard that will land directly in artists' release workflow.

South Korea's KOMCA has walked back its no-AI copyright policy and will now accept registration of AI-assisted works, reversing a ban in place since March 2025. Korean creators can finally register machine-assisted songs — with disclosure attached.

From ElevenLabs' 11 Voices documentary series: artist Sarah, living with MND, uses her cloned AI voice as a working creative material across new mediums. Voice cloning framed as an expressive instrument rather than an impersonation tool.
